tools.name: icp_deep_dive
tools.description: Helps you decide which customers to go after next. You give your best customers, as a list (industry, size, contract value, sales cycle, tech stack, buying trigger, champion title) or in your own words. You get the patterns they share, with ties named as ties, the budget shown as the contract value range seen in your customers, recommendations, and sector notes when your inputs name a supported sector. It works only from what you give and looks nothing up. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Without customers or customer_descriptions, it returns a request for customer data with example input formats. Invalid typed values return a correction error. Use this instead of icp_gap_analysis when you need patterns in supplied customers before comparing them with an ideal profile.

size.description: Format is text. For example, "200 to 500 employees".

acv.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

sales_cycle_days.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

items.description: Format is text. For example, "existing accounting system".

tech_stack.description: Format is a JSON array. For example, ["existing accounting system"].

buying_trigger.description: Format is text. For example, "an audit review due next quarter".

champion_title.description: Format is text. For example, "finance director".

items.description: Format is a JSON object. For example, {"name":"an approved anonymous manufacturer","industry":"manufacturing","size":"200 to 500 employees"}.

customers.description: List of customer objects with available attributes. Format is a JSON array. For example, [{"name":"an approved anonymous manufacturer","industry":"manufacturing","size":"200 to 500 employees"}].

customer_descriptions.description: Alternative: Describe your best customers in text format. Format is text. For example, "manufacturers with 200 to 500 employees".

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge (software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management). Read from your other inputs when left out. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "saas".

tools.name: icp_scoring_model
tools.description: Helps you decide which leads are worth a seller's time. You give the criteria that matter, how important each one is and, if you know it, what goes with success. You get a lead scoring template: example point weights set by importance level, example points for each value you list, a scorecard and tier bands to adjust, with sector notes when your inputs name a supported sector. Your success pattern is matched to your criteria; it does not set the weights. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Without scoring_criteria, it returns a labelled example model. Invalid values return a correction error. Incomplete or failed held_back_test evidence holds the scoring decision. Use this instead of account_prioritization when you need a reusable scoring template before ranking named accounts. Ask for held-back test counts and the pre-agreed stop rule when a model has been tested.

criterion.description: Format is text. For example, "company size".

importance.description: Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "critical".

items.description: Format is text. For example, "200 to 500 employees".

values.description: Format is a JSON array. For example, ["200 to 500 employees"].

scoring_criteria.description: Criteria for scoring with importance levels. Format is a JSON array. For example, [{"criterion":"company size","importance":"critical","values":["200 to 500 employees"]}].

correlation_direction.description: Optional confirmed direction of the success pattern. Ask the user whether the named values correlate with better or worse outcomes before filling this. Overrides word reading; unknown withholds a top-points recommendation. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "positive".

success_correlation.description: What correlates with success? (e.g., "deals with VP Sales champion close 2x faster"). Format is text.

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell, as a product category, so the scoring notes use your sector. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

held_back_test.description: Optional results on deals held back before tuning. Ask for the counts and the stop rule set before the test. A missed rule holds the scoring model; do not tune on this set. Format is a JSON object. For example, {"wins_tested":20,"wins_passing":17,"non_wins_tested":20,"non_wins_passing":3,"minimum_win_pass_percent":80,"maximum_non_win_pass_percent":20}.

wins_passing.description: Format is a whole number. For example, 17.

non_wins_tested.description: Format is a whole number. For example, 20.

non_wins_passing.description: Format is a whole number. For example, 3.

maximum_non_win_pass_percent.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 20.

tools.name: buyer_group_analyzer
tools.description: Helps you decide who else must agree before a deal can close. You give what you sell, the deal size, the company size, your champion and any stakeholders you know. You get a buying group map with your stakeholders placed by their titles (economic buyer, technical evaluator, reviewers, users), each role's concern and message prompts, an influence map and discovery questions, with sector roles and questions when your inputs name a supported sector. Roles from titles are hypotheses to confirm. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of impact_identify_champions when you need a deal buying-group map covering budget, technical and review roles.

tools.name: tam_sam_som_calculator
tools.description: Helps you decide how big your market is, counted bottom up. You give how many companies could buy and your annual contract value in dollars, plus your ICP match rate and year 1 share if you have them. You get TAM, SAM and SOM with the arithmetic and assumptions shown and a summary for an investor deck. It is a calculator, not a data source: a rate you leave out is filled with a labelled example, and sector notes are added when your inputs name a supported sector. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of impact_anchor_market when you have a chosen market and need bottom-up market arithmetic.

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

tools.name: lookalike_signal_generator
tools.description: Helps you decide how to find more accounts like your best ones. You give your ICP's company profile, technologies, champion titles and buying triggers, and optionally what you sell and the platforms you use. You get targeting criteria and search queries for each platform, one signal for each trigger, and search keywords from what you sell and the sector. It writes criteria, not data: it finds no companies or contacts. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of icp_deep_dive when you already have an ICP and need search criteria and trigger signals.

tools.name: account_prioritization
tools.description: Helps you decide which accounts to work first. You give your accounts with fit, intent and relationship scores from 0 to 100 and a timing, plus optional weights. You get a ranked list from a weighted score, with a tier for each account, the points its timing earned and the factor that added the most points. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Without accounts, it returns the scoring framework and an example input. Missing account scores default to 50. Invalid ranges or all-zero weights return an error. Use this instead of icp_scoring_model when you have accounts and numeric scores ready to rank.

fit_score.description: 0 to 100. Left out, 50 is used. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

intent_signals.description: 0 to 100 (0 scores zero). Left out, 50 is used. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

relationship.description: 0 to 100, based on existing connections. Left out, 50 is used. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

tools.name: icp_gap_analysis
tools.description: Helps you decide whether you are selling to the customers you meant to. You give your current customer base, your ideal customer profile and, if you have them, current and target metrics. You get what the ideal profile has that the current base lacks, metric gaps from your own figures, causes to check and actions that fit your business model, with sector notes when your inputs name a supported sector. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of icp_evolution_tracker when you need to compare the current customer base with a stated ideal profile.

tools.name: icp_evolution_tracker
tools.description: Helps you decide whether your ICP should change after recent wins and losses. You give your current ICP, recent wins, recent losses and market changes. You get a candidate change for each (an addition to test, a disqualifier to test, an implication to check), a draft of the updated ICP, the roles your ICP does not name, the loss reasons to tag and what to pull from your CRM. It does not compute win rates; check each candidate against your CRM. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of icp_gap_analysis when you need candidate ICP changes from recent wins, losses and market shifts.

tools.name: icp_interview_synthesizer
tools.description: Helps you decide what your customer interviews mean for your ICP. You give structured notes, one per interview: the customer, the role, pain points, buying triggers, value realized and key quotes. You get the pain points, objections, buying triggers, value realized and champion roles across the interviews, quotes kept word for word, discovery questions and sector notes. It does not take full transcripts; give only the points and quotes you want analyzed. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Without interview_notes, it returns the structured-notes format to supply. Invalid typed values return a correction error. Use this instead of customer_interview_kit when you already have structured interview notes to analyze.
